AimView.description:
Where the pole should go, and how far it is from there.

`x_px` and `y_px` are the aim, which is the center of the reticle. `dx_px` and `dy_px` are the
pole minus the aim, and they are `null` when the pole lies behind the camera.
`distance_arcmin` is the exact angle between the pole and the sky direction at the aim pixel.
AimView.title: AimView

AlignmentFrameInfo.description: The frame that the state describes. Coordinates elsewhere are pixels of this frame.
AlignmentFrameInfo.title: AlignmentFrameInfo

AlignmentStartRequest.description: Start the alignment stream. Leave a field out to use the configured value.
AlignmentStartRequest.title: AlignmentStartRequest

AlignmentState.description:
What the Align page shows next to the live view. The answer of `alignment_state`.

Every part is `null` when `core` does not know it yet, and `quality` says why. `t_utc` is an
ISO 8601 UTC time. Positions are in pixels of the frame in `frame`, so the UI scales them to
the size of the image that it shows. `reticle` is the fixed circle of the first layer, and it
exists without a solution. `sky` is the layer that is fixed to the stars: the pole, the aim, the
orbit of Polaris, and the camera model of the latest current solution. It exists whether or not
a target is set.
AlignmentState.title: AlignmentState

AxesView.description:
The image directions of the two moves of the mount, as unit vectors (x right, y down).

`altitude_*` is where the camera looks when you raise it, and `azimuth_*` is where it looks
when you turn it toward the east. The pole lies on the side of the aim in which the camera has
to move, so the two vectors read like the arrows of a compass drawn on the picture.
AxesView.title: AxesView

BurstRequest.description: Record raw frames to a SER file for `duration_s` seconds.
BurstRequest.title: BurstRequest

CameraView.description:
The camera model of the frame, so that a page projects sky points like the solver does.

`rotation` holds nine numbers, row by row: the rotation from CIRS (the apparent frame of
date) to the camera frame. A sky point `u` projects to `w = R u`, `x = center_x_px +
(w_x / w_z) / s`, and `y = center_y_px + parity * (w_y / w_z) / s`, where `s` is
`scale_arcsec_px` in radians per pixel. A point with `w_z` of 0.05 or less is not in front of
the camera. Pixels follow the frame of `AlignmentFrameInfo`, with the center of the first
pixel at 0.
CameraView.title: CameraView

reason.description: The code of a rejection, or `null`.

DarkLibraryResponse.description:
The dark library, whether it is due for a new set, and the latest dark session.

`mode`, `gain`, and `exposure_s` are the settings of the survey, which a new set should match.
`sets` holds the newest sets first. A value that `core` does not report is `null`, and
`quality` says why.
DarkLibraryResponse.title: DarkLibraryResponse

DarkModelResponse.description:
The dark current as a function of temperature: the rate at the reference and the doubling.

`doubling_fitted` is false while the library holds too few sets for a fit, and the doubling
is then a default.

doubling_c.description: The temperature step that doubles the dark current.
doubling_c.title: Doubling C

DarkModelResponse.title: DarkModelResponse

DarkRequest.description:
Record a dark set with the camera covered. Leave a field out to use the configured value.

The server also holds `exposure_s` to `[web.requests] max_dark_exposure_s` and `label` to
`max_label_chars`, which are settings of the installation.

bias_frames.description: The number of bias frames. `null` uses the configured number.
bias_frames.title: Bias Frames

exposure_s.description: The exposure of a dark frame, in seconds. `null` uses the survey exposure.
exposure_s.title: Exposure S

frames.description: The number of dark frames. `null` uses the configured number.
frames.title: Frames

immediate.description: Start at the next step of the scheduler, because someone stands at the camera with the cover on. A survey exposure in progress finishes first. Without it, the session waits for the next cycle boundary, as the other tasks do.
immediate.title: Immediate

pause_after.description: Pause the scheduler when the task ends, so that nothing records data while the camera may still be covered. `Resume` continues.
pause_after.title: Pause After

wait_for_cover.description: Wait until a test frame is dark, which means that the camera is covered. Without it, the first frame that is not dark ends the task as failed.
wait_for_cover.title: Wait For Cover

wait_for_cover_timeout_s.description: How long the session waits for the cover before it gives up, in seconds. `null` takes the setting `wait_timeout_s` of `[survey.dark]`.
wait_for_cover_timeout_s.title: Wait For Cover Timeout S

DarkRequest.title: DarkRequest

DarkSetResponse.description: One dark set of the library.

rate_e_per_s.description: The dark current, in electrons per second per pixel.
rate_e_per_s.title: Rate E Per S

temperature_c.description: The mean sensor temperature during the set.
temperature_c.title: Temperature C

DarkSetResponse.title: DarkSetResponse

DarkStatusResponse.description: Whether the library needs a new set, and why. `reason` is a sentence.
DarkStatusResponse.title: DarkStatusResponse

DarkTaskResponse.description:
The latest dark session of this `core` process.

`state` is `idle` (none yet), `queued`, `running`, `ok`, `failed`, or `aborted`. While it
runs, `phase` is `bias`, `cover` (waiting for dark frames), `dark`, or `build` (the master
dark and the library), with `step` of `steps` in that phase. `covered` and `level_dn` describe
the latest check of a frame, and `reason` says why a frame was not dark. A finished session
keeps its `summary` (one sentence) and the `set_name` that it added.
DarkTaskResponse.title: DarkTaskResponse

Event.description:
An occurrence that the operator or the analysis may need to see.

`t_utc_ns` is the time of the occurrence. Two events can share a timestamp, so the store moves the later event forward by one nanosecond until its station and time are unique.

detail.description: Structured data about the event, as a JSON object.

kind.description: A dotted code that names the kind of event, such as `scheduler.state_change`.

x-codes.info: A normal occurrence that is worth recording.
x-codes.warning: Something unexpected that the system handled.

message.description: A short description of the event in plain language.
examples: The scheduler entered the auto state.

profile_id.description: The ID of the hardware profile that was active when the record was produced.

provenance.description: The versions that produced the result, as a map from a component to a version string, such as the algorithm revision (`algo`) and the calibration versions.

quality.description: The reason that a value is missing or uncertain, as a map from the field name to a short reason, or `null` when every field is present and trusted.

revision.description: The revision of the result for this station and time, which is 0 for the first result and grows by one for each reprocessed result.

station_id.description: The ID of the station that produced the record, from the local configuration.

t_utc.description: The start time as an ISO 8601 UTC string with six fractional digits. The integer `t_utc_ns` is too large for a JavaScript number to hold exactly, so use this field there.

t_utc_ns.description: The start of the interval that the record describes, or the instant for a point record, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, in UTC.

Pointing.description:
The pointing solution of one survey frame.

`t_utc_ns` is the UTC time at the middle of the exposure. The attitude is a rotation matrix, so analysis can express it in ICRS or in the frame of date. The plate scale belongs to the readout mode in `readout_mode`. A frame that the solver cannot solve has `null` in every geometry field and the `unsolved` flag.

center_dec_deg.description: The declination of the field center, in degrees.

center_ra_deg.description: The right ascension of the field center, in degrees.

flags.description: The conditions that apply to the solution, as documented codes.

x-codes.few_stars: Too few stars matched for a reliable fit.
x-codes.moved: The offset from the reference solution exceeds the configured limit.
x-codes.roll_undefined: The center lies on the pole, so the roll is undefined.
x-codes.time_invalid: The clock was not synchronized, so `t_utc_ns` is not trustworthy.
x-codes.unsolved: The solver found no solution, so the geometry fields are `null`.

n_matched.description: The number of stars that the fit matched to the catalog.

reference_id.description: The ID of the reference solution that `offset_arcmin` refers to.

revision.description: The revision of the result for this station and time, which is 0 for the first result and grows by one for each reprocessed result.

PoleView.description:
Where the celestial pole of date falls. Offsets are the pole minus the frame center.

`x_px`, `y_px`, `dx_px`, `dy_px`, and `distance_px` are `null` when the pole lies behind the
camera. `distance_arcmin` is the exact angle between the frame center and the pole. `roll_deg`
is the position angle of the direction to the pole, from image up toward image left, and it
is `null` within one pixel of the center.
PoleView.title: PoleView

Quality.description: The reason that a value is missing or uncertain, as a map from the field name to a short reason, or `null` when every field is present and trusted. A client reads a `null` value together with this map, which gives the reason as a short code, such as `too_few_frames`.

ReticleView.description:
The fixed reticle: a circle that does not move with the mount.

It is centered on the aim (the center of the frame, unless `[alignment]` names another pixel),
and its radius is the radius of the orbit of Polaris in pixels of the frame:
`tan(colatitude) / scale_rad_px`. It depends on the frame size, the plate scale, and the
colatitude of Polaris only, so `core` serves it without a solution too.
ReticleView.title: ReticleView

SeeingWindow.description:
The seeing statistics of one window of frames, normally 60 seconds long.

`t_utc_ns` is the start of the window. A window never spans a reconfiguration of the camera, so one `stream_id` covers all of its frames. A statistic that the window cannot support is `null`, and `quality` says why.

assumed_wind_ms.description: The wind speed that the estimator assumed for the exposure correction, in meters per second.

background_mean_dn.description: The mean local background, in digital numbers.

centroid_gain_correction_factor.description: The factor by which the estimator multiplied the variance to correct for the difference between the centroid in the finite aperture and the G-tilt.

centroid_noise_px.description: The centroid noise per axis that the estimator subtracted from the variance, in pixels.

detrend_correction_factor.description: The factor by which the estimator multiplied the variance to add back the turbulence that the polynomial detrend removed.

duration_s.description: The length of the window, in seconds.

exposure_correction_factor.description: The factor by which the estimator multiplied the variance to correct for exposure averaging.

exposure_us.description: The exposure time of each frame, in microseconds.

flags.description: The conditions that apply to the window, as documented codes.

x-codes.cloud: Clouds crossed the star during the window.
x-codes.degraded: The system dropped more than 5% of the expected frames.
x-codes.heater_on: The dew heater was on, so heater plumes can add turbulence.
x-codes.partial: The window ended early, for example because the star neared the edge of the ROI.
x-codes.saturated: The star saturated in enough frames to bias the centroid and the width.
x-codes.time_invalid: The clock was not synchronized, so `t_utc_ns` is not trustworthy.
x-codes.twilight: The Sun was less than 18 degrees below the horizon, so sky light can skew the data.
x-codes.vibration: The spectrum shows vibration lines, so the image motion can read high.

flux_mean_e.description: The mean flux of the star, minus the background, in electrons.

frame_rate_hz.description: The mean frame rate during the window, in hertz.

gain.description: The camera gain setting, in the units of the camera driver.

heater_duty.description: The mean duty cycle of the dew heater during the window, from 0 (off) to 1 (always on).

image_motion_rms_x_arcsec.description: The RMS of the detrended centroid along sensor x, with the centroid noise subtracted, in arcseconds.

image_motion_rms_y_arcsec.description: The RMS of the detrended centroid along sensor y, with the centroid noise subtracted, in arcseconds.

motion_psd_dof.description: The degrees of freedom of each bin of the full-resolution image-motion spectrum, which sets the relative scatter of a bin to the square root of 2 divided by this number.

motion_psd_freq_hz.description: The frequencies of the bins of the image-motion spectrum, in hertz.

motion_psd_x_arcsec2_per_hz.description: The power spectral density of the centroid along sensor x in each bin, in square arcseconds per hertz.

motion_psd_y_arcsec2_per_hz.description: The power spectral density of the centroid along sensor y in each bin, in square arcseconds per hertz.

n_dropped.description: The number of frames that the system lost during the window.

n_frames.description: The number of frames that the window analyzed.

outer_scale_correction_factor.description: The factor by which the estimator multiplied the variance to correct for the finite outer scale.

outer_scale_m.description: The outer scale L0 that the estimator assumed, in meters.

peak_mean_dn.description: The mean value of the brightest pixel, in digital numbers.

profile_id.description: The ID of the hardware profile that was active when the record was produced.

provenance.description: The versions that produced the result, as a map from a component to a version string, such as the algorithm revision (`algo`) and the calibration versions.

quality.description: The reason that a value is missing or uncertain, as a map from the field name to a short reason, or `null` when every field is present and trusted.

r0_cm.description: The Fried parameter at 500 nm and at the zenith, in centimeters.

r0_structure_cm.description: The Fried parameter from the structure function of the centroid, in centimeters.

readout_mode.description: The name of the readout mode in the hardware profile, such as `bin1`.

revision.description: The revision of the result for this station and time, which is 0 for the first result and grows by one for each reprocessed result.

saturated_fraction.description: The share of the frames whose brightest pixel reaches 98% of full scale, from 0 to 1.

scintillation_index.description: The normalized variance of the flux, minus the Poisson floor, for the exposure time of the window.

seeing_fwhm_arcsec.description: The Kolmogorov seeing FWHM at 500 nm and at the zenith, from the tilt variance with the outer-scale and exposure corrections, in arcseconds.

seeing_fwhm_structure_arcsec.description: The seeing FWHM from the structure function of the centroid, which ignores slow drift and cross-checks `seeing_fwhm_arcsec`, in arcseconds.

sensor_temperature_c.description: The mean sensor temperature during the window, in degrees Celsius.

station_id.description: The ID of the station that produced the record, from the local configuration.

stream_id.description: The ID of the stream that produced the frames of the window.

t_utc.description: The start time as an ISO 8601 UTC string with six fractional digits. The integer `t_utc_ns` is too large for a JavaScript number to hold exactly, so use this field there.

t_utc_ns.description: The start of the interval that the record describes, or the instant for a point record, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, in UTC.

valid_fraction.description: The share of the expected frames that arrived and passed analysis, from 0 to 1.

vibration_lines_hz.description: The frequencies of the spectral lines that the estimator flagged as vibration, in hertz, or an empty list when it found none.

width_fwhm_arcsec.description: The mean FWHM of the star image, from the second-moment width, in arcseconds.

zenith_angle_deg.description: The zenith angle of the star at the middle of the window, in degrees.

SkyView.description:
The sky layer of the live view: the camera, the pole, the aim, and the move to make.

Everything here is fixed to the stars and comes from the solution of the very frame, so it
moves in the picture as the mount moves. Coordinates are of date. The whole view takes about a
kilobyte, because the state travels with every frame.

`polaris_colatitude_deg` is the angle between Polaris and the pole at the time of the frame,
which is the radius of the orbit, and `orbit` says whether that circle fits in the frame
(`null` without the colatitude). `aim` says where the pole should go and how far it is from
there. `aim_ring` is where Polaris belongs now: the pixel on the circle of the reticle that the
real Polaris would take if the pole sat at the aim, with the same roll and at the same time.
It is the detected Polaris pixel plus the aim minus the detected pole, because the moves of an
altitude-azimuth mount translate the picture.

`altitude_arcmin` and `azimuth_arcmin` are the move of the camera's pointing that brings the
pole to the aim: positive altitude means raise the camera (toward the zenith), and positive
azimuth means turn it toward the east. They are arcs on the sky, so a turn of the azimuth axis
is the azimuth arc divided by the cosine of the altitude of the camera. Both are `null` when
the site is not configured, and when the zenith lies within about a degree of the aim, where
the directions of the two moves are not defined. `axes` holds the image directions of the two
moves, under the same conditions.

info.description:
The REST API of the seeing monitor: a fixed camera that points at Polaris, and a Raspberry Pi that
measures the atmospheric seeing and the sky quality unattended.

**Versioning.** The API lives under `/api/v1`. Within `v1`, a change only adds a field or an
endpoint. A breaking change creates `/api/v2`, and `v1` stays for at least one release.

**Access.** Reads are open on the LAN by default, and a setting can require the token for reads
too. Every `POST` needs the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The server refuses every
command when no token is configured. A client that sends too many requests gets 429 with a
`Retry-After` header.

**Hosts.** The server answers a request only when its `Host` header names an allowed host: the
loopback names, the addresses that the server listens on, and the entries of the `allowed_hosts`
setting. Any other host gets `400 host_not_allowed`, and the message names the setting. A WebSocket
handshake with an `Origin` header needs an allowed host there too. This rule does not change who
may read or send commands.

**Values.** Times are ISO 8601 UTC strings. A field name carries its unit, such as
`seeing_fwhm_arcsec`. A missing value is `null`, and the `quality` object says why. Every error
has the same shape: `{"error": {"code": ..., "message": ..., "details": ...}}`.

**History.** A history route takes `from` (included) and `to` (excluded), and `step` (`raw`, `1m`,
`10m`, or `1h`). A numeric field of a bucket is the mean, and a list of flags is the union. A page
holds at most `limit` items, and `next_cursor` points to the next page.
info.summary: Seeing, sky quality, pointing, images, and commands.
info.title: Seeing monitor API

post.description:
Queue a dark session: record bias and dark frames with the camera covered.

Cover the camera before you send it. With `wait_for_cover`, the session waits until short
test frames are dark, which proves that the camera is covered. The session adds a set to the
dark library, and with `pause_after` it pauses the scheduler at the end, so that nothing
records data while the camera may still be covered. `Resume` (`POST /mode`) continues, and
`Pause` ends a running session as `aborted`. The session starts at the next step of the
scheduler, after a survey exposure in progress, and a paused scheduler or a running alignment
holds it back until you resume or the alignment ends. Only one session may be queued or
running (`409` with the reason `busy`). `GET /dark` shows its progress.
